title: Admin Sentinel: Task-queue runbook runner for lightweight ops automation
creator: Amir Khanna
description:
Problem: Our current set of admin runbooks lives as ad-hoc scripts and long playbooks scattered across docs and repos. On-call engineers repeatedly re-run manual steps, copy/paste commands, and maintain bespoke wrappers for things like tenant drain, model rollback, GPU reboots, and quota resets. This increases MTTR, produces inconsistent audit trails, and blocks our ability to safely automate low-risk operational tasks.

Goal: Build 'Admin Sentinel' — a lightweight, auditable task-queue based runner that treats runbooks as discrete tasks with structured inputs, approval gates, and observable execution. The runner should enable: idempotent steps, parameterized templates, Slack-driven approvals, per-run logging and artifacts (stdout/stderr), automatic retries with backoff policies, and integration with Console telemetry. It must be safe by default (dry-run mode, RBAC checks) and easy for engineers to migrate existing playbooks into tasks.

Design overview:
- Task contract: YAML/JSON manifest with metadata (title, owner, inputs, timeout, required-approvals, artifacts, tags). Tasks can declare steps of type: shell, http, python, terraform, or call existing internal admin APIs. Steps can mark outputs to be persisted to artifacts.
- Runner architecture: small service (ops-sentinel) that consumes tasks from the internal job-queue (we'll reuse Helix-queue), executes steps in an isolated ephemeral container, streams logs to Console (log namespace: ops.sentinel/<task-id>), and writes artifacts to the admin S3 bucket with access controlled by KMS keys.
- Approval flow: Tasks that set required-approvals will pause in 'pending' state and send an actionable Slack message (with inline Approve/Reject buttons). Approvals are recorded in audit log.
- Safety controls: default dry-run for tasks with 'impact: medium/high', RBAC check via org directory (group: ops-admins), rate-limiting by team, and a kill-switch feature that can cancel all running tasks in a region (for emergency).
- Observability: metrics emitted to our prometheus namespace (ops_sentinel_tasks_started, tasks_succeeded, tasks_failed, tasks_approval_wait_time), traces instrumented via OpenTelemetry, and a Console dashboard (link in attachments) showing latencies, failure categories, and top failing steps.

Implementation plan (phases):
1) Prototype (this ticket): build core runner, basic task schema, shell/python step types, log streaming, dry-run, and Slack approval hooks. Deploy to staging. (ETA: 2 weeks)
2) Hardening: add artifact storage, KMS integration, RBAC checks, retries/backoff, and rate-limiting. Add unit/integration tests and chaos scenarios. (ETA: 2 weeks)
3) Migration & Docs: convert 6 high-frequency postmortem runbooks to tasks (drain-tenant, model-rollback, restart-worker, purge-cache, rotate-keys, quota-adjust), author on-call cheat sheet, runbook quickstart for engineers. (ETA: 1 week)
4) Canary rollout: route internal admin traffic to Admin Sentinel for low-impact tasks, monitor Console SLOs, then expand.

Trade-offs & alternatives considered:
- Build vs reuse: We evaluated adopting the existing 'opsplaybook' project but found it tightly coupled with a legacy datastore and CLI. Building a focused runner reduces long-term technical debt and avoids migrating heavy state.
- Queue choice: Helix-queue chosen for operational familiarity and multi-region support; Redis streams was considered but would require additional HA effort.
- Execution sandbox: containerized execution chosen for step isolation. We considered running steps directly on host but rejected due to security and auditability.

Testing & validation:
- Unit tests for parser/manifest validation and approval gating.
- Integration tests that simulate step failures, network partitions, and KMS errors.
- Post-merge e2e run that executes a 'no-op' dry-run task in staging and verifies logs/artifact flow and Slack approval behavior.

Rollout & migration notes:
- Begin with read-only tasks (reporting, diagnostic data collection) to validate execution model.
- Migrate repeatable, low-risk runbooks first (ex: 'collect-diagnostics').
- Maintain legacy scripts for 2 weeks behind feature flag while updating runbooks and runbook owners.

Security & compliance:
- All artifacts encrypted with customer-admin KMS when sensitive.
- Audit log entries for every task state transition and approval.
- Security review required for tasks that manipulate secrets (flagged during manifest validation).

Deliverables for this ticket:
- ops-sentinel service scaffold + CI, Helm chart for staging, task schema spec, Slack approval integration, Console telemetry hooks, and a staging demo with 3 example tasks.

Next steps: assign infra to provision Helix-queue topic for staging, request S3 prefix + KMS key from Security, and schedule a demo with on-call and SRE teams.
acceptance_criteria: Runner can successfully execute a parameterized task in staging and stream logs to Console
Slack approval workflow functions end-to-end (approve/reject recorded in audit log)
Artifacts from a task are stored with KMS encryption and retrievable via Console
Metrics (started/succeeded/failed) visible in Console dashboard and alertable
RBAC checks block a restricted task when run by a non-admin user
